units.author: sb_bins
units.text: Wendell, keep a dated log, as I did. Collections, times, the registration of the lorry, and whether the lids went back on. They cannot argue with a log. I see from this morning's Weyhaven paper that you already do, and that the city is to review it. Well done. Bernard (Rope Walk)

units.author: dc_3_wendell
units.text: Thank you Bernard. The reporter rang me and I read her the log down the phone, all four months of it. She stopped me in August. I had more. The council will 'report early next year', which in my experience means late next year. I will keep writing.

units.author: skeptic_planner
units.text: Part 2 of the survey is now up at the Society (costs). Note 5a is the line people will quote: the engineer advises daylight working only and recommends against extending the clearance beyond the tower strip. Read in context, it's a costing note. Winter days are short, contractors charge for boats. The Courier has run it this morning, fairly, I thought.

units.author: truthwatch_gil
units.text: 'Would not recommend that the clearance strip be extended beyond what the tower requires.' In 1953 an engineer says don't clear more of this island than you have to. In 2024 or whenever, someone pays a fortune to clear all of it in a month. You call that a costing note. I call it a warning nobody listened to. A private refuge for the rich needs nothing around it, that's my view.

units.author: skeptic_ferrous
units.text: Gil, if he'd meant 'warning' he had a whole report to say so in. He was a Board engineer writing to a Board that wanted to spend as little as possible. 'Don't clear more than you need' is what every engineer says about every site. It's also what I'd tell a client who wanted the work priced keenly.

units.author: hollow_signal
units.text: Gil's closer than he knows. The relay wasn't cancelled for staffing... people at the Board knew what the Holm was for even then. I'm not able to say more on an open forum. Some of us have been tracking this a lot longer than a month.

units.author: sb_mod
units.text: HollowSignal, if you have a source, please post it. If you can't post it, please don't hint at it. Members have asked repeatedly. I'll leave the post up this time. Pell (admin).

units.author: hist_wiki_marsh
units.text: For those reading the survey closely: the engineer's daylight-only line is consistent with a note in our 1923 naturalist's notebook, also newly up, that her boatman insisted on taking her off by half past four. It's consistent, not confirming. Boatmen in the Sound have refused to stay out after dark for as long as there have been boatmen. [citation needed on that last sentence, I admit].

units.author: propwatch_ledger
units.text: Finding 4, with thanks to planning_portal_watcher: the Tollinby sawmill that held the Holm from 1961 was dissolved in 1998, but the land stayed with a family member's estate until the recent sale. Nobody felled a tree on it for sixty-odd years. I had assumed a timber company would cut its own trees. Apparently not this one. Not sure what it means yet.

units.author: skeptic_planner
units.text: It probably means the sawmill bought it cheaply as a reserve and then went out of business before it needed the reserve, which happens. Access was always the problem. You'd need a landing, a barge and a crew willing to camp, and the trade was never short of trees on the mainland.

units.author: skeptic_brisk
units.text: Lads it's an island. A rich bloke bought an island. He wants a view. That's it. Seventy-year-old paperwork about a lighthouse that never got built is not a conspiracy, it's a filing cabinet.

units.author: gilliver_lamp
units.text: Bram's grandad's brother was Eddie Rendle, he rowed for the Board men that year. I remember him a little. He used to say they were nice gentlemen who ate a great deal of cake. My mother gave them tea in our front room once when the boat was late. They sat with their coats on. I don't know why I remember that, it was a long time ago.

units.author: ex_grieve_corran
units.text: I took the location out of my old post for a reason. I'm not going to put it back in because someone on a forum says I owe it. I worked for them, they paid me, I left. Some of us came back from up there and some of us came back different. That's all. I won't go into it.

units.author: sb_mod
units.text: Thank you for saying so. Members, please respect that. Any further questions to this member about his former employment will be removed. Pell (admin).

units.author: sb_commuter_lisle
units.text: Day two of the new timetable. 07:10 out of Lisle took the long way round the spit because of the buoy, six extra minutes, missed my bus at Ammet by one. They've announced an extra 18:45 'crew permitting'. Translation: we have found someone who isn't being reviewed. I'll believe it when I'm on it.

units.author: skeptic_ferrous
units.text: The buoy deviation is sensible, Ewan. The east cardinal is off by 80 metres; if the skipper cut the corner and the buoy is wrong, so is he. I'd rather lose six minutes than a hull plate. The tender is re-laying it tomorrow on the flood, according to the Coastguard.

units.author: parent_tollinby
units.text: Update for anyone in the same boat (sorry): my sister made the 20:15 and the bus, just. She says the boat was rammed and very quiet, nobody chatting like usual, everyone just looking at their phones or out of the window at the dark. She said it felt like the last train home after something bad has happened, then laughed at herself.

units.author: sb_commuter_lisle
units.text: That matches. I was on it last night too. Packed, and you'd think a packed boat would be noisy. It wasn't. The crew were doing everything twice. Lights on the car deck all the way across, which they don't normally bother with. Probably just being careful after the storm.

units.author: lisle_crew_ada
units.text: Lisle pier tonight: 20:15 came in at 20:52 with the long way round, nobody fell in, everyone thanked me for the gangway like I'd built it. ha. The slip lights are all working. I didn't look at the end of it. I'm just saying that, I didn't.

units.author: wx_carrowpoint
units.text: 07:00 readings. Pressure 1021.3 hPa, a steep rise overnight. Wind calm, 0 to 2 knots. Grass minimum minus 3.8 C, air minus 0.6 C at the station. Hoar frost on the salt crust on the windward posts, which looked rather pretty. Visibility 35 km. Expect cloud from the south tonight and a damp, misty start tomorrow, dew on everything.

units.author: wx_carrowpoint
units.text: 20:00 readings. Pressure 1019.0 hPa, starting to fall slowly. Wind S 3 knots. Temperature 5.2 C, dew point 4.6 C, so very little gap: dew forming on the station roof already. Visibility down to 12 km and dropping. The kind of night where you hear the Lisle pier generator from here. Mist by midnight, I'd say.

units.author: lineman_tess
units.text: Dew on top of storm salt, isn't that the bad combination you mentioned? Garvey just groaned when I read him this. We're on standby tonight for the coast lines. I'll make a note of what time anything trips, if anything does, and compare against your readings after.

units.title: Trades & Jobs: storm work, fully booked.
units.author: trades_holm_work
units.text: Thanks all for the calls after my post in the storm thread, I'm now fully booked to the end of next week with windblow in tollinby and brackwater. If you need a fallen tree cleared I can put you on a list. Taking on a labourer with a CS30 if anyone knows a lad. Day rate good, home every night!

units.author: parent_tollinby
units.text: Davey, put me on the list please, Orchard Close, small cherry across the back fence, nothing dramatic. Also 'home every night' is a strong selling point this week, you might want to put it in bigger letters.

units.author: fisher_bram
units.text: Good lad Davey. Glad you've found work on this side. Plenty of it after a blow like that, and you sleep in your own bed. That's worth more than an island rate.

units.title: Local Oddities: people in the reservoir woods at night.
units.author: brackwater_keeper
units.text: Not an oddity, a nuisance, but this seems to be where people read. Last night I counted three cars in the reservoir car park after eleven. The recording folk, who stayed where they said and were off by four, I've no complaint about. The other car was someone filming with a light on his head, shouting into his phone below the dam. The paths are closed and flooded. Stay out.

units.author: nightscream_vlog
units.text: guys that was me lol, I was doing a scouting run for the big Brackwater livestream, it's going to be insane, the knocks are REAL I heard two of them myself just below the dam. full stream coming soon, link in bio, sorry about the shouting I get excited

units.author: brackwater_keeper
units.text: You were standing on the outflow pipe. What you heard was air in the outflow pipe, which is running full since the storm. If I find you below the dam again after dark I'll be ringing the police, not your phone.

units.author: skeptic_brisk
units.text: 'The knocks are real' says the man standing on a pipe. Mate, honestly. Grow up and stay out of the woods.

units.author: dunlin_rec
units.text: For what it's worth, the keeper's right about the pipe: we logged those outflow thumps from the dam road last night and they're clearly the pipe, with the spillway running. They also sound quite different from the knocks in the woods, which is a separate question. Our files will be on LowBand. Make of it what you will.

units.title: Front Row, Gilliver: after the water.
units.author: retired_teacher
units.text: I went across on the morning boat to help my friend on Front Row lift her carpets. Two cottages had water through the door and one cellar is still a paddling pool. The council engineer was very pleasant and wrote everything down. If anyone has a dehumidifier they could lend for a week, Front Row would be grateful, and I will vouch for its return.

units.author: gilliver_lamp
units.text: Thank you Mrs Hale, you were a great help with the rugs and you were quite right about the corner one, it was ruined. The young man from the Courier asked me about the lamp and I told him what I always say, it's only manners. I hope he puts it in properly. The water is out of my hall now.

units.author: harbourmaster_quill
units.text: The harbour office has a dehumidifier and two pumps that can be borrowed by Front Row residents free of charge. Please call at the office during opening hours. Thank you to Mrs Hale and to everyone who has been helping. It is very much appreciated.

units.title: done
units.author: deckhand_finn

edit.text: handed my notice in today. not going into why, it's personal and it's not the company's fault. thanks to Odell and Kerris and everyone on the boat, best crew I've worked with. I'll be around the harbour. don't message me about it please.

units.text: handed my notice in today. people keep asking so here it is. it's not the rota and it's not the money. Kerris saw it on the slip, everyone knows that. what people don't know is I saw it too, two nights before the storm, on the late run in. not at the end of the slip. on the steps, halfway up, closer to the boat than I am to my front door. I put the deck light on it and it didn't move and it didn't look at the light. I didn't say anything because of the jokes. I'm not doing nights again. thanks to Odell and Kerris.

units.author: harbour_admin
units.text: sorry to see you go Finn. you're a good deckie. lads, he's asked not to be messaged, so don't. if anyone gives him grief at the harbour they'll get it from me.

units.author: lisle_crew_ada
units.text: Finn... I read the first version before you changed it. I'm not going to repeat any of it. I just want to say I believe you and I'm sorry about the jokes, I made some of them, before mine. Look after yourself.

units.author: fisher_bram
units.text: There's always work on the boats if you want days, son. Ask on the quay. Nobody'll ask you why.

units.author: lineman_tess
units.text: Don't know you but good luck. I'm on standby on the Gilliver line tonight and I'll be up by the harbour some of it, so if you see a yellow van by the slip it's just me, not anything to worry about.

units.author: deckhand_finn
units.text: thanks Bram. might take you up on that, days only though. I'll come down the quay at the weekend and find you.

units.author: ferry_mate_kerris
units.text: Crew note for the quay: the extra 18:45 depends on us finding a deckhand by tomorrow morning. If you're ticketed and can do days and early evenings, ask at the office. Before anyone asks, I'm staying, I'm on days, and my account of the slip hasn't changed: dark coat, no light, too tall for a kid.

units.author: ferry_engineer_seth
units.text: We're doing the engine-room side of the review this week, which mostly means me filling in a form about how many hours I've spent in a hot metal box. Answer: lots. If they want to improve my welfare, a working kettle on the lower deck would do it.

units.author: ferry_skipper_odell
units.text: We're a deckhand down from today. I won't discuss why; it was his decision and a fair one. The 18:45 runs if we fill the post. Kerris has said what she saw, and I've said what I logged. Neither of us has added to it, and we won't. Carried on.

units.author: harbourmaster_quill
units.text: Thank you, skipper. A reminder to all harbour users that the slipway lighting has been checked and is fully working after the storm. Two extra lamps have been fitted at the top of the Gilliver slip steps this week, for safety, as requested by Sound Lines. Thank you.

units.author: fisher_bram
units.text: Went in at low water this morning and fetched the four creels off the Holm north shore, first light. All fine, one with a crab in it looking pleased with itself. You could hear a saw going up in the trees already and a radio somewhere. Somebody's working hard over there. Price up a bit at the merchant's today, the lorry got through.

units.author: harbour_admin
units.text: glad you got them back. still no sign of the green rowing boat, coastguard reckons it went east of the harbour mouth. if it fetches up on the Holm the island lot are welcome to it, it leaks.

units.author: lineman_garvey
units.text: Back on standby tonight, coast lines this time. Weather man says dew on top of storm salt and I believe him, that's when insulators flash over. If anything goes tonight it'll be along the Gilliver feeder by the sea wall where the spray got it worst. Washing those strings is on next week's list, which is one week later than I'd like.

units.author: ferry_engineer_seth
units.text: If the Gilliver end goes, the terminal shore power goes with it and I have to start the boat's genset to keep the lights on at the berth. Not complaining, just warning you I'll be ringing to complain. Pint stands.

units.title: Session night 4 (the calm one): files and sync sheet
units.author: dunlin_rec
units.text: Files up: three positions, 22:00 to 03:50, clocks synced and rechecked (offsets on the sheet, all under 0.2 s). Spillway ran all night. Summary: the outflow pipe thumps are clearly the pipe, every few minutes, low and boomy. Separately, two single knocks from the wood side at 02:12, dry and high, no answer from tern's position. Otherwise, nothing. Six hours of nothing, which is also a result. Kit: two omnis, dish, handheld. Make of it what you will.

units.author: tern_audio
units.text: ok so confirming: pumping house position got the pipe thumps, nothing at 02:12, and an awful lot of owl. I checked my clock against the radio signal at 04:00 and it was 0.1 s out, which I have written in pen on the sheet so nobody can say anything. also the soup was a success.

units.author: hobby_binaural
units.text: Headphones on: Gerald caught the 02:12 knocks faintly, both from the front-left, which lines up with the woods side of the dam path and not with the pipe, which is behind-right of him. Gerald also caught me sneezing at 01:03, sorry about that. Raw file up, unaltered.

units.author: skeptic_hollis
units.text: Quick analysis. Pipe events: energy mostly 40-120 Hz, slow decay, irregular spacing of 3 to 6 min. That's air slugs in a full outflow, as expected. The 02:12 pair: broadband, sharp onset, peak around 1.8 kHz, very short decay. They're not the pipe. They look like something hard striking wood. A person with a stick fits. So does a branch falling onto another branch after a storm.

units.author: dunlin_rec
units.text: Agreed on both, and thank you. A falling branch is very plausible after three days of gales. The only thing I'd add is that two of them, 1.4 s apart, in still air, is a bit tidy for branches. But tidy isn't evidence. I'll go back in daylight and see if anything is freshly down on that side.

units.author: skeptic_hollis
units.text: Good plan. Separately, on tern's file from the first session night, the one people are calling voice-like: I've been trying to make water hammer fit it. The pipe was nowhere near full that night, and the bands in it move in a way pipe resonance shouldn't. I'm not done. I'll post when I am.

units.author: hobby_hydrophone
units.text: Branch, or a gate. Is there a gate in the woods on that side? A gate latch in still air carries a long way and comes in pairs, open and shut. Most of what I record in the harbour turns out to be a gate or a pump.

units.author: brackwater_keeper
units.text: There's no gate on that side. There's a stile and a fence and three hundred acres of trees. I came by at eleven like I said and listened on their headphones. Heard owls and the pipe. I'll give them this, they were where they said.

units.author: lowband_mod
units.text: Pinning this. This is what a session write-up should look like: positions, sync, raw files, and a result that includes six hours of nothing. Thank you all.

units.title: Brackwater 'teaser' (re-upload)
units.author: nightscream_vlog
units.text: BRACKWATER TEASER guys!! put together the best bits from the LowBand session files with my own scouting run footage, added a bit of atmosphere so you can really feel it, this is the real deal, full livestream coming, link in bio, share it everywhere, credit to the recording guys obviously

units.author: lowband_mod
units.text: Removed. This is the third time you've re-uploaded other members' files with music added, after a final warning yesterday. NightScreamLive is temp-banned for fourteen days. dunlin_rec and tern.audio, I've passed the link to you in case you want it taken down elsewhere. Thread locked.

units.author: tern_audio
units.text: ok so thank you. he put a heartbeat sound under my pumping house file. there is no heartbeat in my file. there's an owl and a pipe. I've reported it on the video site as well.

units.author: hobby_tapeloop
units.text: I have listened to last night's files against my reservoir tape of 1974. The pipe thumps are, to my ear, very like the bulk of what is on my tape, which supports my view that it records the dam works. I confess the two sharp knocks at 02:12 are not on my tape at all. Regards, Ned.

units.author: dunlin_rec
units.text: Thank you Ned, that's really useful. If the pipe was making those noises in 1974 as well, it's good to have that on the record. I'll ask the archive whether your tape can be filed next to last night's for anyone who wants to compare.

units.title: Standing at the edge of the light
units.author: lh_lighttender_tamsin
units.text: I tend one of the last staffed lights on this coast. From the gallery at night you see the beam go out over the water and come back across the headland path. Tonight, as on a few nights before, there was someone standing on the path just where the beam stops reaching, past the last fence post. I always take it to be a walker. Walkers here are patient people. It was there through four sweeps of the light and then it wasn't, and I went on with the lens.

units.author: lh_callcentre_tamsin
units.text: lamp_and_lens I love your posts but please never describe my coast like that again while I'm on a night shift. also sorry, three callers in a row tonight about storm damage to their fences, as if a utilities helpline can do anything about a fence. one of them was crying about the fence. it was a really nice fence apparently.

units.author: lh_mod
units.text: Housekeeping: I've let this stand as its own thread because it's a first-hand report with a time and a place, which is what we ask for. Please keep replies to your own experiences, not other threads. And as ever: company, not campfire stories. Ines.

units.author: skeptic_dmitra
units.text: A rotating beam is almost a recipe for this. Your eyes adapt to the light on each sweep and then to the dark between, and the boundary of the beam is exactly where contrast is worst. Something at the edge gets a few hundred milliseconds of light per sweep. A post, a gorse bush, a walker. I'd be surprised if keepers didn't see figures there.

units.author: skeptic_orla
units.text: I'll say it gently because I like lamp_and_lens: 'standing at the edge of the light' is now a phrase. It's on three threads here, it was on our overnight show last week twice, and once a phrase exists people start fitting their nights into it. A walker on a headland is the most ordinary thing in the world. Let it stay a walker.

units.author: lh_miner_vellmark
units.text: Underground the old men keep inside the lamp's circle. Habit. You don't step where you can't see your boots. Nothing more to it. Off shift now. Bus is cold.

units.title: bus depot tonight, a small one
units.author: dc_5_lorna
units.text: Not much of a story love but I'll tell it, at twenty past three I was doing the back row at the depot and one of the double deckers at the far end had all its inside lights on, upstairs and down, and the doors shut, nobody on it, and I thought well somebody's left it on after the storm like they did all week, so I went to switch it off and by the time I got to it the lights were off and the cab was cold and the key wasn't in it, and the fitter says they go off on a timer, which I'm sure they do

units.author: lh_security_st
units.text: Lorna, they do. The newer ones have a battery-saver that kills the saloon lights after a set time, usually 20 or 30 minutes after the ignition's off. If the cleaners had it on earlier and it timed out just as you got there, that's your answer. Control agrees, and Control never agrees with anything.

units.author: dc_5_lorna
units.text: Thank you love that's a comfort, and tell Control thank you, though I'll say I was the cleaner on that row and I hadn't been in it yet, but there's plenty of others on nights and somebody must have been, it's a big yard

units.author: lh_picker_weyhaven
units.text: Depot's across the road from our yard and I can see that back row from the smoking shelter. Didn't notice tonight, I was busy being yelled at about lines per hour. Will look tomorrow on my break. If a bus turns its own lights on I want it on our team, it shows more initiative than the agency lot.

units.title: night run oddity (a nice one, mostly)
units.author: lh_porter_portammet
units.text: Taking an old gent from A&E up to the ward tonight, lovely man, bit confused, fell over in his garden in the dark. Halfway up in the lift he asks me if I know a Tomas who works the trees on the island. I said I know a lot of people but not that one. He said 'tell him to keep the light on' and then asked for a cup of tea like nothing had happened. Nurses say he used to fish out of Gilliver. Tea delivered. Back on the run.

units.author: lh_nurse_halvard
units.text: They do that, the confused ones at night, they give you messages for people. We had a lady last month who asked me to tell her sister the bread was in the oven. Her sister had died in 1980. You say you will, and you mean it, and it settles them. Sounds like you did right. Back to it.

units.author: lh_insomniac_tollinby
units.text: There's a whole old tradition of the confused and the dying carrying messages, in the books at least. I hope he sleeps. There must be a dozen Tomases working outdoors in the Sound, and every one of them could do with being told to keep a light on in November.

units.author: lh_porter_portammet
units.text: Ta, that's what I did. Said I'd pass it on. He's asleep now, snoring like a trawler. Vending machine on B corridor is dispensing hot chocolate that tastes of soup tonight, if anyone's wondering about the state of the NHS.

units.author: lh_trucker_orrin
units.text: Seen plenty of folks stand just off the lights at truck stops. Usually they're smoking where the manager can't see, or on the phone to someone they don't want overheard. Or they're waiting on a ride that's not coming. Go out with a coffee one night and ask him. Ten to one he's got a story and it's a sad one. Keep your thermos full, driver.

units.author: lh_convenience_kestrel
units.text: good idea. I'll take him a coffee. if he's a ghost he gets a coffee, if he's a man he gets a coffee. nobody loses. he's not out there yet tonight. it's raining a bit. maybe he doesn't like rain. me neither.

units.author: lh_student_kestrel
units.text: update from the lab: the motion lights in our corridor are behaving since facilities changed the sensor, I have written 600 words of chapter 4 (progress!!) and I bought a coffee from taro and the forecourt was empty. sorry to everyone waiting for the forecourt man. he is not my responsibility. my thesis is.

units.author: lh_kennel_orrin
units.text: Late to this but: cold pizza, standing up, because Biscuit the spaniel is on a post-op watch and won't settle unless I'm in sight. We have nine boarders tonight. Dexter the old lab wouldn't go down the back corridor again at two, sat right down at the corner. I took him round the other way. He's fine. I'm fine. Pizza is fine.

units.author: lh_baker_coriveth
units.text: End-of-batch heel of a seeded loaf with salted butter, which is the best food in the world and nobody can change my mind. Also tasted the first attempt at a new rye. Too sour. The starter is sulking after the cold snap. Starters are like people at four in the morning, they need warmth and patience.

units.author: lh_taxi_halvard
units.text:
that sounds better than my kebab
quiet night, three hospital runs and a woman who wanted to go round the ring road twice because her baby only sleeps in a moving car
baby slept
she slept
I did not sleep, I was driving
anyway best tip of the week

units.author: dc_7_irena
units.text: Dear neighbours, thank you Bev for opening a new place to talk, and for the conditions, which my late husband would have approved of; he could not abide a quarrel on a landing. I have nothing new to report except that the lift has worked for five days and I have used it every time. Irena, 7C

units.author: dc_5_lorna
units.text: Morning Irena love, I came in at five as usual and took the stairs as usual, all the way to 5, and not a sound as usual, which I keep saying is the strange part, all the noise people talk about and I never get any of it, maybe it's a night person thing and I'm a morning person now, I'll pop up with your paper later

units.author: dc_14_ivy
units.text: Following the rules: first hand, my own ears. Last night at 02:20 I heard steps go up past my door (14, top floor) and keep going up the last half-flight to the roof door. Then nothing. No door. I didn't open mine (I'm brave in drawings only). I've sketched the landing with the roof door in it, which I'll describe as: a door, very shut, looking smug.

units.author: dc_6_jordie
units.text: ivy I was up at that time last night and I didn't hear anyone come up past 6, and you'd have to come past 6 to get to 14 unless you took the lift, and the lift was on 1 because I could hear it. so either it walked up from 7 or my ears are rubbish. could be my ears tbh I had headphones on half the night.

units.author: dellow_admin
units.text: Update from me: Kerrow rang back today (a first) and said the relay part has arrived at their contractor and they'll confirm a date tomorrow. I'll believe it when I see a van in the car park. Residents' meeting next week as planned. Thank you all for keeping this thread civil so far. Bev, DCRA.

units.author: dc_9_tobin
units.text: Noted. When the relay is fixed I propose a control recording: same time, same descent, lights fully on. 1. If the excess steps persist with lights on, the lighting is irrelevant. 2. If they stop, the dark was doing something to how we hear. Either result is useful. Benedikt, you would not have to take part.

units.author: skeptic_hollis
units.text: Good design. I'd add one thing: record a known walker descending while a second person stands still on a landing two floors above, so we know what a stationary listener's breathing and shifting sound like on the recording. A lot of 'extra steps' in stairwells turn out to be the recordist.

units.title: Free to a good home: kids' things
units.author: dc_11_soraya
units.text: Having a clear-out. Free to anyone in the building: a bunk bed ladder (no bed, long story), a blue scooter that R. has outgrown, two bags of picture books, and a nightlight shaped like a moon that little M. says he doesn't need any more. Flat 11F, knock after six. We won't need much where we're going, I'll explain to Bev.

units.author: dc_7_irena
units.text: Dear Soraya, I would very much like the picture books for my great-niece, if no one with small children needs them first. I hope everything is all right with you and the boys. You know where I am. Irena, 7C

units.author: dc_2_hassan
units.text: Soraya, if you need boxes I have plenty from the deliveries, good strong ones from the tinned stock. Come down any time and take what you want. No need to explain anything. H

units.author: dc_11_soraya
units.text: Thank you both. Irena, the books are yours, I'll bring them down. Hassan, yes please to boxes, about ten. Everything's fine, really, just a change. Sorry to be mysterious. I'll say properly once it's sorted.

units.author: dc_2_hassan
units.text: Today: fresh bread, and the newspaper with Wendell in it, page nine, about the bins. I have put a copy in the window. Also the delivery van will come at 05:30 from now on instead of 04:00 because the driver says he does not like waiting in our car park in the dark. Fine by me, I get more sleep. H

units.author: dc_3_wendell
units.text: Hassan, please take the paper out of the window. I said what I said and I stand by it, but I do not need it in a window. Also please tell your driver that the car park is perfectly safe and the only problem with it is people parking across three bays.
